links.outcome: Usability and workflow integration barriers reported by ED clinicians using RAPIDx AI
links.effect: Novice users faced usability and workflow integration barriers; residents/interns had the lowest comprehension (median 0.198) and emotional engagement (median 0.112). Experienced clinicians suggested automation and streamlined workflows.
links.quote: Novice users faced usability and workflow integration barriers, while experienced clinicians suggested automation and streamlined workflows.

links.outcome: Comprehension and usability differences by user experience level
links.effect: Registrars had the highest comprehension (median 0.466); residents/interns the lowest (median 0.198). Novices had usability challenges and needed targeted training.
links.quote: RAPIDx AI enhances diagnostic accuracy and efficiency for experienced users, but usability challenges for novices highlight the need for targeted training and interface refinements.

unlisted_practices: Using a Bayesian expert-elicitation framework (PROLIFERATE_AI) to score AI usability and adoption by user role

screen.reason: Evaluates the clinical workflow integration and usability barriers of the RAPIDx AI decision support tool across 12 emergency departments using human-centered evaluation methods.
